Schema **1.2 → 1.3**. Groundwork for N→N finding capture: the record has to hold the fields before verifiers can fill them.

## Measured before

Across the repository, exactly **one** of twenty-six `Gate.fail()` call sites emitted a command a reader could paste — and it was inside `how_to_fix` as a sentence. Every other one said some version of *"fix the code, not the gate"*.

## Added — all keyword-only, all defaulted

| field | why it wasn't there |
|---|---|
| `finding_id` | **derived**, not passed — a caller free to choose it could give two defects one handle |
| `severity` | defaults to `ERROR`, which is what a recorded failure always meant here |
| `code` | `what` is a sentence; a rule id is a key you can search docs with |
| `file` / `line` / `column` | the machine form of `where`, which stays free text because gates use it for non-positions (`specs/a.lean + proofs/a.lean`) |
| `root_cause` | why the finding exists, vs `why` = what the tool printed |
| `reproduction_command` | a command, not a sentence about one |
| `is_root_cause` / `dependent_on` | verifiers run under one `set -e`; the first failure stops the rest, and those are not independent defects |
| `merge_blocking` | stated per finding, not inferred from a gate status two files away |

The five originals stay **positional and unchanged**, so all twenty-six call sites read exactly as they did. That is what makes this a minor bump rather than a rewrite of every verifier in one push.

## Why 1.3 is MINOR

Fields are added to entries in `failures[]`, none removed. Every 1.2 consumer still reads a 1.3 report, and `aggregate_gates.py` compares only `SCHEMA_MAJOR`. Top-level `required_fields` are untouched — none of the new fields is top-level.

## The log, not just the artifact

A field that exists only in an artifact nobody downloads is a finding the system discarded. Fields with a `None` value are **omitted**, not printed as `column=None`, which would read as a measurement whose value happens to be None.

## One existing test failed, and it was the right one

`test_the_schema_minor_moved_and_the_major_did_not` pinned `"1.2"` as a literal. It now reads the version from `ci/gates.toml` — the manifest is where the version is *declared*, and a test asserting its own copy of a number proves the two agree with the test rather than with each other.

## Tests — 12

every declared field present · optional fields recorded as given · **an omitted field is `null`, never invented**, so "nobody measured a column" stays distinguishable from "the column is zero" · severity defaults to ERROR · a dependent finding points at its root · **the id matches the finalizer's** and is stable across runs · two defects get two ids · every new field reaches the log · no field printed as `=None` · and the control: the original five-argument form still works

## Evidence

full suite exit 0 · **and again with `GITHUB_SHA`/`RUN_ID`/`RUN_ATTEMPT`/`WORKFLOW` set to CI-shaped values, exit 0** · pyright 0 errors · gate_integrity 0 · registry_gate 0

No verifier's exit code, threshold or judgement changes. This is what a finding *is*, not what counts as one.
